svg.text: Not to scale. Front plate pulled down and forward, back plate back, sides, top and bottom out; braces in place. Biscuit slots shown on the visible faces.
All panels from one board (cutting plan). Measure the OSB first; check the plates'
diagonals — they set the box square.
Recess Ø267 × 4.5 with a router and circle jig (test in scrap with a driver),
M5 inserts on Ø250, then the Ø231 cutout. Ø20.5 gland hole in the back.
Two coats of thinned lacquer on the inside faces. Mask the glue faces and slots.
48, size 20 (sheet 2). Reference from the face; check every slot for voids.
Front plate face down; glue sides, top and bottom onto it with biscuits,
strap-clamped. Dry-fit the back to hold it square.
Window brace flat, top face 330 below the top (spacer blocks), glued to all four
walls. Tie strip on edge, centred, 155–195 below the top, glued to the front.
Acrylic bead in every inside corner you can reach now.
Glue on with its biscuits and glue on the tie strip's end. Strap + cauls.
Bead the back corners through the driver holes.
Sand 80 then 120, 2–3 coats of clear water-based lacquer, as Le Petit.
Gland in, 4-core cable through, sealed. 300–500 g wool through the holes:
lower half and corners, a hand's width free round each basket.
+ to + on both. Battery test: both cones move out. Gasket, M5 × 16, crosswise.
Push a cone in gently: it should come back slowly. A quick return = a leak.
M5 threaded inserts for wood (Ø6.5 drill)
gasket tape, 3 × 10 mm foam (2 × Ø250 rings)
M20 cable gland + 4-core speaker cable, 2.5 mm²
loose wool fill (sheep's wool or polyester)
PVA glue, clear lacquer, acrylic sealant
sealed, ≈ 40 l net · 2 × SB Acoustics SB26SFCL38-4, opposed · companion to Le Petit
22 mm OSB · biscuits (size 20) + wood glue · glued shut, drivers from outside
